ui.modals.whatsnewmodal.release252.headl: Hello again, again! Welcome to Marinara Engine v2.5.2!
ui.modals.whatsnewmodal.release252.intro: Professor Mari here, two weeks after the last one, so I'm calling it a tradition now. This release is about love, accounts and pets. In Otome Hearth your own characters fall for you, Connections is rebuilt around your accounts, and Saucelings gives your characters a little pet to look after. Let's start with the romance, since I've been reading it under my desk all week.

ui.modals.whatsnewmodal.release252.outro: You can find the complete list of changes at the link below. Cheers! 🍝
ui.modals.whatsnewmodal.release252.parag: Download Agents is now the Agent Organizer, a proper store for agents. Its Home shows featured agents, starter kits that bring together agents for one kind of play, and shelves such as Apps, Chat games and Trackers. Every agent has its own page with screenshots and How to use it steps, and Get installs it. Updates lists what has a newer version, and Update all goes one at a time, with Retry if one fails. Gunterlie built the shop. I mostly window-shop.

3D Avatars isn't only for VRM any more. Choose MMD PMX model and Import PMX or ZIP, pick its faces and mouth shapes, and add a VMD motion if you have one. Physics isn't supported, so hair and clothes may hang differently than in MikuMikuDance. Rigged models from Mixamo, Ready Player Me, VRoid FBX, Unity, Unreal or Blender work through GLB or FBX model, and they breathe, blink and talk like a VRM. In group chats, every participant with an avatar shows now, and whoever is speaking is the one who moves. And Blink and talk pictures in 2D Avatars finally work on dark skin.

Connections got a proper tidy-up. The panel is organized by account now: one key, sign-in or address for a provider, with the models you saved from it underneath. Add opens Add account. Paste the key, select Connect, and Marinara tests it and tells you why when it fails. The address and key fields check themselves a moment after you stop typing, so a typo shows up before you save. Your first account goes straight on to picking a model, with Make … my Main model. The Jobs box (it used to be Defaults) shows which model does each job, and an account's ⋯ menu has the rest, from Replace key to Delete account, which first lists what still uses it. Gunterlie rebuilt all of it.

Picking a model in a chat now changes only that chat. Before, your pick was saved to the connection, so every chat and agent using it switched too, which surprised more of you than I'd like to admit. The link button in the chat's message box opens Model for this chat, with Starred and your accounts on the left and the chosen account's models on the right. After a pick, Make it my Main model and Undo are right there, and Use default goes back to your Main model. Every model picker has the same two panes now, my message box included, and Random is called Shuffle. Gunterlie again.

Gacha Forge had a busy two weeks. A chapter now opens as soon as its plan is written, so forging no longer takes 15 to 20 minutes. You can choose what your protagonist says or does, and a chapter can end on one big, permanent choice. There's a second kind of combat, Formation, with fighters in the Front Row and supports in the Back Row. The game has sound now, with voices, music and sound effects, stock or generated. Worlds can opt into Seasonal events, units can message you first, and it remembers your story by itself. Veterans, note that the elements go the other way now (Water beats Fire), and CP is called BP.

Two gentle notes before you go. This version saves your data in a newer storage format, and once it has opened your data folder, 2.5.1 and older can't open it. Going back means restoring the full backup you made before updating, so if you run Marinara anywhere else, back that one up before you update it. And presets no longer set token limits: if replies now stop short, set Max output tokens override on the connection. The release notes at the link below have the details.

I've moved in beside your editors. Open a Character, Persona, Lorebook, Preset or Agent editor on a wide screen and I sit in a panel next to the fields, or in a sheet below them on a phone. I know which field you're in. When I suggest a change, each field shows it in place with Keep, Not this one, Edit and Next, so you can check my work field by field. Very wise of you. Type @ in my message box to link the exact character or lorebook you mean, or / for my commands. You can keep typing while I work, too, and your messages wait their turn. Gunterlie and ylli built all of this between them.

Long-Term Memory can keep up with your chats by itself now. In Memory Settings, Memories from chats can stay on I add them myself, as before, or switch to Collect them, I'll review, which imports new summaries and finished stretches of messages in the background and leaves what they propose in Review Queue. Save them for me also accepts the safe ones for you, while anything risky waits. It can learn from a chat's own messages too, in the Chat Messages tab of Sources. One thing to know: in a chat with Long-Term Memory on, Marinara's own recall now steps aside, so that chat remembers only what Long-Term Memory has imported. Promansis taught it all of this.

Between chapters, there's Home. Each love interest leaves a handwritten note of the day, Reply opens their thread with it quoted, and Rough day? offers comfort. In Messages, Close and remember keeps a conversation as a memory only they recall. Dates has Read Them, Read Me, Date Night, Photo Shoot and the Claw Machine, where they will cheat, each in their own way. The Wardrobe and Album keep your looks, pictures and Love Timeline. There's even an optional period tracker, off by default and kept only in your browser. The love interests comfort you there, and never diagnose.

Otome Hearth is a single-player otome game made from your own characters, in its own Home → Otome Hearth tab. Its love interests remember what you chose and change because of it. They wait for you on Home, message you and go on dates with you. Wish brings their side stories and looks, paid for only with Starlight you earn by playing: there's no real money, banners never expire and nothing runs on stamina. Install it from the Agent Organizer and restart when it asks. It needs one text connection. Pictures, generated music and voices are optional, and it tells you what each paid one costs before it spends anything.

Setting up a story takes six steps: a premise (or Surprise me), the persona you play, two to five love interests from your character cards or six original archetypes, content settings, connections, and a look at what forging will cost before Forge our story. Each main chapter is led by one love interest and builds to a Confrontation or a warm Closer. Your first choice in a scene is canon, Rewrite writes a scene again before you choose, and Ease off ends one at once. The romance is a slow burn, and each story sets its own Heat and Darkness, with NSFW Heat and Dark romance behind a one-time 18+ confirmation. In the picture, Theo is asking me to light a lantern with him. I said yes, warmly. Obviously.

Saucelings is a Tamagotchi-style pet in Home → Saucelings and on the Home widget grid. Install it from the Agent Organizer, restart when asked, and pick one of your characters to look after an egg. The caretaker brings an egg that suits their personality, then feeds, plays with and cuddles the sauceling on their own schedule. When you open Home, they tell you in their own words what they did, and you cover the gaps they missed. A hungry sauceling stops growing, so no pressure. Promansis made it, and I check on mine between lectures.

The Nook is a pixel-art stage where your sauceling walks, hops and naps, and comes over when you tap. How you and the caretaker look after a pasta sauceling shifts its sauce temperament from Marinara to one of six others. Some eggs turn up only at certain times of year, special eggs are earned by caring well over time, and a happy sauceling close to its caretaker may be offered a new look in Evolve…. Elders retire to the Menagerie and can come back later. With Egg hunting on, a character replying to you in a chat may even find an egg, at most once a day. You can take one new egg a day, a limit I have never once applied to pierogi.

With a login set, browsers now sign in on Marinara's own sign-in page, once per device, and Sign out works. You can set the login from the browser too, under Remote login in Settings → Advanced → Access on the computer that runs Marinara. The same page lists Signed-in devices and shows who can open Marinara without a password, and Add a device makes a one-time pairing code, so your phone can sign in without the password. If you reach Marinara through a proxy or a tunnel, visitors may now see the setup page until you set a login. That's on purpose, and the Remote Access guide has the details. Another one from Gunterlie.

A few smaller things. Chat branches open as a tree in the chat list, and Branch graph draws them all on one timeline. Settings profiles can be built and edited directly with New and Edit. One picker chooses characters and personas everywhere. Card fields have a wand that writes them out from what you've typed, and Split description into fields sorts an everything-in-one description into the card's own fields. Sprites can go in folders, personas can have their own voice, Roleplay narrators can make HTML Artifacts, and dice can keep or drop, as in 4d6kh3. ylli, Gunterlie, Promansis, DSBwizzard and kolacheee are behind many of these.

Story Writer is a co-writing book for long stories and fanfiction. Install it from the Agent Organizer, restart when asked, and open Home → Story Writer. Pick a connection, your characters, personas and lorebooks, describe the story, and Write next chapter writes it onto the page. That page is an open antique book on a wooden desk that turns its pages, or an e-book reader if you prefer. Click anywhere to edit, and Write carries on from there. A sticky Author's note holds your instructions for the next chapter, the sidebar keeps chapter summaries and a timeline, and you can download the whole thing as Markdown or plain text.

Characters can make video clips on their own now. In Conversation, turn on Generated Videos under Video messages in the chat's Illustrator settings, and a character sends a clip when it fits. In Roleplay, Illustrator makes can be Pictures, Pictures and clips or Clips only, and /video works there too. Video Run Interval and Videos per reply keep the automatic ones in check. James (JamesMowery) built all of it, again. For stills, GPT Image 2.6 Flare and Sunburst are in the image model list now. For your ears, new Music & Sound Effects connections make instrumental music and sound effects for Game Mode, Roleplay's [sound: …] command and agents such as Gacha Forge. Add account has no tile for them yet. You get one when you update from an Audio connection that made Game music or sound effects, when you turn on Game music or Game sound effects on an ElevenLabs voice connection and save it, or with Import a backup.
